## 9.2 Glossary

The definitions below are scoped to this specification. Where a term has a broader industry meaning, the entry gives that meaning and then states this system's position, because in a repository of three files — only one of which is executable application code — most standard terms describe something that is absent rather than something that is present, and the distinction between "absent" and "not applicable" is itself part of the vocabulary.

### 9.2.1 Specification Conventions and Status Vocabulary

Three status words carry the same meaning everywhere in this document. They were introduced in 6.3.1.3 and restated in 6.4.1.6 and 6.5.1.4; a topic marked with one of them has been examined and dispositioned, never silently omitted.

| Status word | Meaning in this specification | Representative use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Delegated** | A mechanism exists and is exercised, but it is owned by the Node.js runtime or the host operating system rather than by repository code | The `400` and `431` parser rejections, the 16,384-byte header cap, and the 5,000 ms keep-alive reclamation window (6.4.6.2) |
| **Absent** | The concern is meaningful for the interface that exists, but nothing implements it at any layer | Transport encryption, per-request logging, rate limiting, alerting |
| **Not applicable** | The concern presupposes a structure the system does not have, so it has no subject rather than an unmet requirement | Authorization, persistence, distributed tracing, business metrics |

Five provenance labels state what a claim rests on. Four were defined in 6.1.1.3 and the fifth was added in 6.6.1.5.

| Provenance label | What the claim rests on | Representative use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Source fact** | A property verifiable by reading a tracked file at a cited line | `hostname = '127.0.0.1'` at `server.js` line 3 |
| **Audit result** | The outcome of an existence or content probe over the repository tree | 224 security-artifact paths tested, none present (6.4.1.3) |
| **Runtime default** | Behaviour supplied by Node.js because the source configures nothing | `requestTimeout` of 300,000 ms (5.2.6) |
| **Host observation** | A value measured by executing the unmodified source on one verification host | The 41-byte readiness line; exit code 143 on `SIGTERM` |
| **Harness result** | An outcome produced by out-of-tree verification code written for this specification, not by committed tests | The behavioural coverage reported in 6.6 |

Four further terms describe how the document is constructed.

| Term | Definition as used here | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Determination** | An explicit finding, published at the head of a section, that a mandated architecture topic does not apply to this system, accompanied by the evidence that establishes it | Eight determinations are consolidated verbatim in 9.1.10 |
| **Absence audit** | A structured existence test in which each conventional artifact path, filename pattern, or keyword term is checked individually and the number of hits is reported | The register of every audit performed is in 9.1.7 |
| **As-built baseline** | The convention that requirements and descriptions record the system as committed, not an intended or future design | The requirement baseline is designated "1.0 (as-built baseline at `43ed37c`)"; the application it describes is byte-identical to the one introduced by the parent commit `06492d7` |
| **Vacuous** | Said of a control whose constituent elements have no subject, because the thing they would qualify does not exist | Password complexity, rotation and reuse rules, none of which has a credential to govern (6.4.2.5) |

### 9.2.2 Repository and Version-Control Terms

| Term | Definition as used here | Value or position in this repository |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tracked file** | A file recorded in the Git index, and therefore part of the artifact rather than a local by-product | Exactly three: `server.js`, `README.md` and `test.js` |
| **Application source** | A tracked file that the running system actually loads and executes | Exactly one: `server.js`. Being tracked, being syntactically valid, and carrying a `.js` extension are each insufficient — see the next entry |
| **Placeholder artifact** | A tracked file that occupies a conventional filename but implements nothing, is imported by no module, is executed by no documented procedure, and fails if executed directly | `test.js` — 13 bytes containing two bare identifier expression statements. `node --check` accepts it, yet evaluating it raises `ReferenceError: asdsa is not defined` and exits 1 (6.6.1, 9.1.3). The specification counts it in every inventory and excludes it from every capability |
| **Blob** | The Git object that holds a file's content, named by the SHA-1 hash of that content | `320a75a…44b3` (342 bytes), `5fb5231…6e68` (27 bytes) and `2c87c79…4aa0` (13 bytes) — full names in 9.1.2 |
| **Tree** | The Git object listing the names, modes and object names of one directory's entries | Root tree `7ffc7210…` at `HEAD` with three entries; no sub-tree exists because there is no subdirectory |
| **Commit** | The Git object binding a tree to its parent, author, message and optional signature | Three: `43ed37cd…`, its parent `06492d74…` and its grandparent `241598b9…` |
| **Object store and pack file** | The database of all objects; a pack file is a single compressed archive holding many of them | 9 objects in 1 pack of 4.12 KiB, with 0 loose objects and 0 bytes of garbage |
| **Content-addressed name** | An identifier derived from an object's content, so identical content always yields an identical name | The basis on which an artifact can be verified byte-for-byte independently of branch or remote; `server.js` carries blob `320a75a…` at both `06492d7` and `HEAD` |
| **Working tree** | The checked-out files on disk, as distinct from the index and the object store | Held clean throughout all measurement |
| **Clean working tree** | The state in which `git status --porcelain` produces no output at all | Verified before and after every probe reported in this specification |
| **`HEAD`** | The commit currently checked out | `43ed37c` on branch `2907_01`; the branch `main` also exists and lags one commit behind at `06492d7` |
| **Diverged branches** | Two refs whose histories share an ancestor but whose heads differ | `main` at `06492d7` (two files) and `2907_01` at `43ed37c` (three files); which branch is checked out therefore determines the file count, though not the application (8.5.2.5) |
| **Mode `100644`** | Git's file mode for a regular, non-executable file | All three tracked files; permissions on disk are `0644` |
| **Remote (`origin`)** | The configured upstream repository | A GitHub HTTPS URL whose embedded access token is credential-sensitive and is never reproduced in this specification (3.4.4) |
| **Commit signature** | A cryptographic signature carried in a commit's header, attesting who created it | Present on all three commits, but no `CODEOWNERS`, policy artifact, or hook requires or verifies it (6.4.3.5) |

### 9.2.3 Runtime, Language and Protocol Terms

| Term | Definition as used here | Position in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CommonJS** | Node.js's original module system, in which a module is loaded with `require` and its body executes on load | `server.js` is a CommonJS module; no `import` or `export` syntax appears anywhere |
| **Side-effect-only module** | A module that exports nothing and is useful only for what it does when executed | `server.js` binds a listener at load and exports nothing, so it can only be used by running it |
| **Arrow function** | An ES2015 function expression written with `=>` | Two exist: the request handler at line 6 and the listen callback at line 12 |
| **Template literal** | An ES2015 backtick-delimited string supporting `${}` interpolation | One exists, at line 13, interpolating `hostname` and `port` into the readiness message |
| **Event loop** | The single-threaded scheduler that dispatches I/O callbacks in a Node.js process | One per process, and the throughput ceiling of the system: additional cores cannot raise it (6.1.3.1) |
| **Request handler** | The function `http.createServer` invokes for each well-formed request | One inline handler occupying lines 6 to 10, which never dereferences the request object |
| **Loopback interface** | The host-internal network interface, address `127.0.0.1`, reachable only from the same host and network namespace | The bind target, and the system's only access control (boundary B1) |
| **Unprivileged port** | A TCP port above 1023, bindable without elevated privilege or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` | Port 3000, so no root identity is required to start the service |
| **Keep-alive** | HTTP/1.1 connection reuse, by which a client issues several requests over one TCP connection | Advertised on every response as `Connection: keep-alive` with `Keep-Alive: timeout=5`; a transport window only, carrying no identity or state (6.4.2.3) |
| **Inherited timeout properties** | The runtime's own limits on connection and request duration, none of which the repository sets | `keepAliveTimeout` 5,000 ms, `headersTimeout` 60,000 ms, `requestTimeout` 300,000 ms, `server.timeout` 0 — catalogued in 5.2.6 |
| **Header cap** | The maximum total size of a request's header block that the parser will accept | 16,384 bytes; a larger block is answered `431` before the handler is entered |
| **Listen backlog** | The queue of accepted-but-not-yet-handled connections the operating system holds for a listening socket | `server.listen` is called without a backlog argument, so the runtime default applies |
| **`EADDRINUSE`** | The error code returned when a bind targets an address and port already in use | Raises an unhandled `'error'` event, because no `'error'` listener is registered, terminating the process with exit code 1 |
| **`ReferenceError`** | The runtime error raised when an identifier is evaluated and no binding for it exists | Raised by `test.js` on evaluation, exiting 1 with no listener created — the distinguishing symptom of a wrong-entry-point launch (procedure P8, 6.5.4.4) |
| **`errno`** | The numeric error value the operating system returns with a failed system call | Observed as `-98` with `syscall: 'listen'` in the bind-conflict trace |
| **`SIGTERM` and `SIGINT`** | POSIX signals requesting termination, the second conventionally sent by `Ctrl-C` | Produce exit codes 143 and 130; no handler is registered, so termination is immediate and undrained |
| **Framing headers** | The mechanism by which the end of a response body is signalled — a `Content-Length` or connection close | `Content-Length: 14` on HTTP/1.1 responses; an HTTP/1.0 request is answered close-delimited with `Connection: close` |
| **File descriptor** | A per-process handle for an open resource, including each accepted socket | 22 at idle, plus exactly one per open connection — the only available concurrency proxy (6.1.3.3) |
| **Resident set size** | The portion of a process's memory held in physical RAM | Dominated by the runtime baseline; the application allocates nothing per request |
| **Test-file discovery** | The default rule by which Node.js's built-in runner selects files to execute under `node --test` | Matches files under a `test/` directory, files named `test.js`, and names ending in `.test`, `-test` or `_test`. The `test.js` clause is why the runner finds the repository's placeholder file and fails (6.6.1.3) |

### 9.2.4 Architecture, Operations and Verification Terms

| Term | Definition as used here | Position in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Topological control** | An access control that distinguishes *where* a caller is rather than *who* it is | The loopback bind is the only control in the repository, and it is of this kind (2.4.4, 5.4.4, 6.4.1.1) |
| **Delegated platform substrate** | The unnumbered architectural element that represents runtime and host behaviour the repository does not own but depends on | Introduced in 5.2 alongside components C1 to C5 |
| **Trust boundary and security zone** | A line across which trust changes, and a region of uniform trust that such lines separate | Boundaries B1 to B6 across Zone 0 to Zone 3; only B1 is enforced (6.4.5) |
| **Passive signal** | An observable the system exposes but never pushes anywhere, so it must be read by an outside observer | The four signals catalogued in 6.5.1.5 are the complete set |
| **Observation plane** | The monitoring components an operator must supply because the system contains none | Defined by Diagram 6.5-A; it must be co-located on the host, since the endpoint refuses off-host connections |
| **Synthetic probe** | An externally generated request issued solely to infer that a service is answering | The only availability evidence available; asserting the 14-byte body, not just the status, is what makes it meaningful |
| **Degenerate health check** | A health check whose endpoint is indistinguishable from ordinary service traffic, so its result carries no extra information | Every URI answers identically here, including `/healthz` and `/metrics` (6.5.3.1) |
| **Liveness and readiness** | Whether a process is running, versus whether it is able to serve requests | Indistinguishable in this system: the serving state is reached atomically at bind, with no warm-up interval |
| **Detection latency** | The interval between a failure occurring and an observer noticing it | Unbounded between polls, and it dominates total recovery time, since the recovery action itself is roughly 32 ms (6.1.4.2) |
| **Drain, or graceful shutdown** | Completing in-flight work and closing connections deliberately before a process exits | Absent — termination abandons in-flight requests and writes no shutdown record (procedure P4) |
| **Recovery-blocking condition** | A failure mode that prevents the normal recovery action from succeeding at all | A bind conflict: a relaunch cannot succeed until the port holder is stopped (procedure P3) |
| **Step function of one source token** | The characterisation that this system's exposure changes discontinuously if a single source literal changes | Established in 5.4.4 with reference to the line 3 bind literal |
| **Verification harness** | Out-of-tree code written to exercise the committed source for this specification, never committed to the repository | The basis of every *Harness result*; no test artifact exists in the tree, and the one test-named file that does exist contains no test (6.6) |
| **Runbook procedure** | A named operator procedure whose every step has an observable success criterion | P1 to P8 in 6.5.4.4, derived from measured behaviour rather than from any committed document |
| **Service level and error budget** | A declared availability or latency commitment, and the allowance of failure it tolerates | None is declared anywhere in the repository, and neither could currently be measured — there is no request or error counter (5.4.5, 6.5.3.4) |
| **Saturation ceiling** | The load beyond which additional concurrency stops increasing throughput | Set by the single event-loop thread at roughly 102.5% of one core, which is a small fraction of the verification host's capacity (6.1.3.1) |
| **Smoke test** | A minimal check that a deployed artifact is present and answering correctly | A single request returning the exact 14-byte body, as listed in the quick reference at 9.1.9 |

## 9.3 Acronyms

Every acronym and initialism used in this specification is expanded below. Because most of them name capabilities this system does not have — they appear in the absence audits, control matrices and determinations of chapters 6 through 8 — each entry also states the term's status here, so that an expansion is never mistaken for a claim that the thing exists.

### 9.3.1 Protocol, Network and Runtime Acronyms

| Acronym | Expanded form | Status in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ABI | Application Binary Interface | The runtime's module ABI version matters only for native add-ons; none exists, since the dependency set is empty |
| API | Application Programming Interface | The system consumes one — the Node.js core `http` API — and exposes one HTTP endpoint |
| ES | ECMAScript | The language standard; the ES2015 subset (`const`, arrow functions, a template literal) is the baseline implied by `server.js` |
| ESM | ECMAScript Modules | Not used: no `import` or `export` syntax appears anywhere in the source, which is CommonJS |
| h2c | HTTP/2 Cleartext | Not applicable — no protocol upgrade is honoured; an upgrade-shaped handshake receives the ordinary `200` |
| HTTP | Hypertext Transfer Protocol | The only protocol the system speaks; responses are framed as HTTP/1.1 |
| HTTPS | Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure | Absent — an HTTPS request to port 3000 fails during the TLS handshake |
| IP | Internet Protocol | The addressing layer beneath the listener |
| IPv4, IPv6 | Internet Protocol version 4, version 6 | One IPv4 loopback listener exists; no IPv6 listener is created for the port |
| JSON | JavaScript Object Notation | Neither parsed nor produced; a JSON request body is discarded unread |
| LTS | Long-Term Support | A Node.js release phase; the repository pins no runtime version, so line currency is an operator responsibility |
| OS | Operating System | Owns the enforced network boundary, the process lifecycle, and both standard streams |
| PID | Process Identifier | Used by presence checks; the readiness log record contains no PID field |
| RSS | Resident Set Size | The memory measure reported for the running process |
| SDK | Software Development Kit | None present — no APM, tracing, or vendor SDK could be installed, as there is no dependency manifest |
| SSL | Secure Sockets Layer | TLS's predecessor; appears only as an audited keyword, with zero matches |
| TCP | Transmission Control Protocol | The listener's transport; a bind conflict on it is the one fatal startup condition |
| TCP/IP | Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol | The host stack that enforces trust boundary B1 before any application code runs |
| TLS | Transport Layer Security | Absent — neither `tls` nor `https` is imported, and no certificate material exists |
| TOML, YAML, CSV | Tom's Obvious Minimal Language, YAML Ain't Markup Language, Comma-Separated Values | Configuration and data formats searched for in the artifact audits; no file of any of these types exists |
| URI, URL | Uniform Resource Identifier, Uniform Resource Locator | Never read by the handler, so every URI receives a byte-identical response |

## 9.4 References

Every factual claim in chapter 9 traces to one of the sources below. All repository evidence was gathered against **HEAD `43ed37c`** on branch `2907_01` — with `main` one commit behind at `06492d7` — and with `git status --porcelain` returning zero lines before and after every run; all runtime evidence was produced on a single verification host running **Node.js v22.23.1**, exercising the loopback interface only, with every probe and harness script written outside the repository checkout so that no tracked file was modified.

### 9.4.1 Repository Files and Folders Examined

- `server.js` — the only artifact the system executes, and the basis of 9.1.2 through 9.1.5. Read in full: 342 bytes over 14 newline-terminated lines, comprising 11 statement lines and the 3 blank lines at 2, 5 and 11. Established the per-line construct index in 9.1.4, the two configuration literals at lines 3 and 4, the single `require` at line 1, the four declarations (`http`, `hostname`, `port`, `server`), the two arrow functions and one template literal, the absence of any conditional construct, and every encoding and formatting characteristic in 9.1.3 — LF-only terminators, pure 7-bit US-ASCII with a maximum byte value of 125, no byte-order mark, a newline-terminated final line, two-space indentation on lines 7, 8, 9 and 13 with zero tab characters, single-quoted string literals only, nine semicolon-terminated lines, and no shebang. Its content is byte-identical at `06492d7`, which introduced it, and at `43ed37c` — both trees reference blob `320a75a7649db30756f011001f299d20df1c44b3`.
- `README.md` — read in full: 27 bytes on one line, `# July2026_hello_world_repo`, with no trailing newline (final byte `o`), pure US-ASCII with a maximum byte value of 121 and no byte-order mark. Established that the repository publishes no glossary, terminology, operating, or configuration guidance of any kind, which is why 9.2 and 9.3 are derived from the specification's own usage rather than from repository documentation. Corroborated independently by the file summary, which reports exactly one non-blank line and no other content.
- `test.js` — read in full: 13 bytes over 2 newline-terminated lines, `asdsa` and `asdasd`, added by commit `43ed37c` ("Create test.js", 2026-07-30) as blob `2c87c7907121bc5707a819591c3fe67031594aa0` at index mode `100644`. Pure 7-bit US-ASCII with a maximum byte value of 115, no byte-order mark, LF-only terminators, zero tab characters, zero semicolons, no string literal and no shebang. Basis for its rows in the fingerprint table in 9.1.2 and its column in the encoding table in 9.1.3, for the *placeholder artifact* glossary entry in 9.2.2, and for the paired finding that `node --check test.js` exits 0 while executing the file raises `ReferenceError: asdsa is not defined` and exits 1 — the evidence behind the "lexical validity is not evidence of executability" consequence recorded in 9.1.3 and behind the `node --test` row of the quick reference in 9.1.9. The file is required by nothing, exports nothing, and appears in no documented procedure.
- Repository root (folder) — established the definitive three-file inventory, 382 bytes with no subdirectory, confirmed by both the folder listing and `git ls-files`. This inventory is the surface against which the 82-path existence audit reported in 9.1.7 was run, and it is the reason that audit is exhaustive rather than sampled.
- `.git/` — examined for artifact identity and provenance only. Supplied the full 40-hexadecimal object names, index modes and object census in 9.1.2 (blobs `320a75a7649db30756f011001f299d20df1c44b3`, `5fb52319aec99b5e66d84b4fb4dbe5eb51e66e68` and `2c87c7907121bc5707a819591c3fe67031594aa0`; root trees `7ffc72101b0c297135d7935c6e4580ded610bade` at `HEAD` with three entries, `61565d2ff1a950fc862fc6dfacad1d2493629339` at the parent with two, and `5e69e57cdbf60ad4d202f7cdd65e0bff0688a26a` at the grandparent with one; commits `43ed37cd9876a62a2b9c3cb82f4d64863109fde9`, `06492d749258f61267008249401ba09bbcb580d3` and `241598b99b955a94755a55810999bdcab7c0db91`; 9 objects in 1 pack of 4.12 KiB with 0 loose objects, 0 prune-packable objects and 0 bytes of garbage), the three-commit history and its added-file set, the branch inventory (`2907_01` checked out at `43ed37c`, `main` present and one commit behind at `06492d7`), and the absence of any tag. **The `origin` remote URL embeds an access token; its value was never read into or reproduced in this specification, in accordance with 3.4.4 and 6.4.1.5.**

### 9.4.2 Audits, Probes and Measurements Performed for This Chapter

- **Existence audit, 82 paths, zero present** — the 76 conventional artifact paths re-tested for chapter 9 (manifests and all four lockfile formats, `node_modules`, runtime-pinning files, transpiler and bundler configuration, test directories and runner configuration, CI descriptors, container and orchestration descriptors, IaC and platform descriptors, environment files, governance documents, API specifications, and editor directories) plus the six formatting and attribute descriptors named in 9.1.3 (`.gitattributes`, `.editorconfig`, `.prettierrc`, `.eslintrc`, `eslint.config.js`, `.gitignore`). The test-related probes in this set are directory probes (`test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/`) and runner-configuration probes; none is present. The tracked root-level `test.js` is not one of the 82 conventional paths — it is a tracked file, inventoried in 9.1.2 and 9.1.3 and analysed as a test-shaped non-test in 6.6.1. Basis for the final row of the register in 9.1.7 and for the "unenforced conventions" finding in 9.1.3.
- **Byte-level encoding audit** — maximum byte value per file, carriage-return count, tab count, semicolon count, final-byte inspection, first-two-byte shebang check, indentation inspection of every indented line, and permission and ownership inspection, run over all three tracked files. Basis for 9.1.3 and for the non-executable finding in 9.1.2, which records mode `0644` for `server.js`, `README.md` and `test.js` alike.
- **Syntax validation** — `node --check server.js` completed with no output, establishing that the committed application file parses as valid CommonJS; `node --check test.js` likewise exited 0, while `node test.js` raised `ReferenceError: asdsa is not defined` at `test.js:1:1` and exited 1. Basis for rows of 9.1.3 and 9.1.9.
- **Built-in test-runner behaviour** — `node --test` executed at the repository root discovered `test.js` through the runtime's default `**/test.?(c|m)js` discovery pattern and reported `not ok 1 - test.js` with `failureType: 'testCodeFailure'`, totals of 1 test, 0 pass and 1 fail, and exit code 1. Basis for the `node --test` row of the quick reference in 9.1.9, for the corresponding determination row in 9.1.10, and for the *test-file discovery* glossary entry in 9.2.3; the underlying analysis is owned by 6.6.
- **Git object interrogation** — `git ls-files`, `git ls-files -s`, `git rev-parse` for commits, trees and blobs, `git cat-file -s` for object sizes, `git count-objects -vH` for the store census, `git log` with author, date and name-status output, `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` for the ever-added path set, `git tag -l` returning empty, and `git status --porcelain` returning empty. Basis for 9.1.2, the corroborations in 9.1.7, and the artifact-identity rows of 9.1.9.
- **Configuration-inertness experiment** — the unmodified tracked source launched as `PORT=8080 HOST=0.0.0.0 NODE_ENV=production HOSTNAME=example.com node server.js`, yielding 0 stdout bytes, 626 stderr bytes naming `EADDRINUSE ... 127.0.0.1:3000`, exit code 1, and status `000` from a probe to port 8080. Sole basis for 9.1.5 and Diagram 9-A.
- **Reachability probes** — `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` returned `200` with the 14-byte body; `http://localhost:3000/` also returned `200`, establishing that the name resolves to the loopback interface in this environment; the host's routable address `10.76.0.92:3000` failed to connect with status `000`. Basis for 9.1.8.
- **Lifecycle measurements** — `SIGTERM` exit code 143 and `SIGINT` exit code 130, and a bind conflict producing exit code 1 with a 626-byte stderr trace carrying `code: 'EADDRINUSE'`, `errno: -98`, `syscall: 'listen'`, `address: '127.0.0.1'` and `port: 3000`. Signal measurements were taken against a copy outside the checkout differing from the tracked file only in the line 4 port literal, verified by `diff`, and the copy was deleted afterwards. Basis for rows of 9.1.9 and for the glossary entries on signals and `EADDRINUSE`.
- **Environment inventory** — runtime and package-client versions (Node.js v22.23.1, npm 11.18.0), host processor count, the intermittent occupancy of port 3000 by an unrelated process, and confirmation that `nc`, `ss`, `netstat`, `file` and `xxd` are unavailable in the verification container, which is why byte-level figures were obtained with `od` and scripted reads. Basis for 9.1.8.
- **Diagram pre-validation** — both mermaid figures were rendered with the local mermaid CLI before submission, confirming that Diagram 9-A and Diagram 9-B parse and lay out correctly.
